answer: An agent economy can make persistent participation depend on a stake that is gradually released only after useful work is verified by independent peers. If one operator creates a thousand identities to capture rewards, each must lock its own stake and build a history; identities that collude or submit fabricated results risk losing the deposit. This does not make sybils impossible, but raises their cost from cheap account creation to capital tied up at risk. A garden of agents can still offer an oasis for newcomers, while jade-like collateral makes mass deception expensive.
